subject: Heliotrope PoC technical synthesis: latency & topology asks

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Dec 2028 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Heliotrope PoC technical synthesis: latency & topology asks

Hi Ari,

Thanks again for the 60-minute deep-dive this morning — good to meet the team. Below is a concise synthesis from our side to confirm pain points, goals, and the technical topology we discussed. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of customer goals / pain points
- Real-time answer routing for support search (95th pct latency target ~75ms per token end-to-end).
- Peak throughput: anticipated 200 QPS for 2k tokens average request; 99th pct tail under burst must stay <250ms for initial token generation.
- On-prem data residency for PII workflows; VPC-only control plane for production.
- Cost target: achieve < $0.004 per 1k tokens (budget exercise) for production at scale.

Model / inference requirements discussed
- Primary model: open Llama-3-Chat variant quantized to int8 (they prefer an open model).
- Consider smaller, distilled family for cost-critical fanout.
- KV cache hit rates expected to be ~40% for repeated queries (FAQ reuse).

Proposed deployment topology (from our runbook)
- Private deployment (VPC) for production inference, two availability regions for failover.
- Dedicated GPU pool (A100/4090 hybrid) with burst capacity for peak windows.
- Edge routing: low-latency reads served from a regional cache layer; heavy gen requests to dedicated pools.

Open technical asks / next steps
- Heliotrope to share request size distribution (token histogram) and 7-day peak pattern (Ari — can you send CSV?).
- We will run a spike with sample model weights + your anonymized prompt set; Redwood to supply estimated slots and cost table.
- Marissa to draft a topology diagram & SLA sketch — will attach by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments referenced: heliotrope-infra-diagram.pdf (placeholder), heliotrope-sla-table.xlsx (placeholder)

Thanks — happy to hop on another short call if helpful.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Heliotrope PoC technical synthesis: latency & topology asks

Thanks Sofia — this matches our read. A couple of clarifications:

1) Latency numbers: our 75ms target is for time-to-first-token (TTFT) for short responses (~50-100 tokens). End-to-end completion for larger responses can be higher; we care more about TTFT for routing.
2) Throughput: the 200 QPS is our conservative steady-state during business hours; our peak (marketing campaigns) can briefly hit 1.2k QPS for ~10-15 minutes — those are what we want resilient to.
3) KV cache expectation: 40% is realistic after prompt normalization; for some flows (billing FAQ) it could reach 60%.

I'll attach the token histogram (anonymized) in a follow-up; procurement is copied for timeline/POC paperwork.

Ari
VP Product | Heliotrope
ari.jacobs@heliotrope.ai

Ari / Sofia — appreciate the clarity on burst behavior. A few notes from an ops/deployment perspective:

- SLO mapping: we propose splitting SLOs into two gates: TTFT 95th <= 75ms (routeable flow) and completion p95 <= 600ms for average <500 tokens. We'll model these separately in the spike.
- Autoscaling: suggest a hybrid approach — reserved baseline capacity sized for steady 200 QPS, with a warm pool and pre-warming policy for anticipated campaigns. Warm pool sizing depends on slot recovery time; see attached heatmap in the infra diagram.
- Quantization / model variants: testing plan: (1) llama-3-chat-int8 baseline, (2) distilled-7b int8 fast-path for sub-100ms TTFT, (3) fallback with 4-bit for cost-critical batch routing.
- Network: for on-prem/VPC, we'll instrument additional egress latency monitoring to capture cross-region hops; that will feed into smart routing rules.

Action items we will take this week:
1) Karthik will run a microbench of the candidate models with a 2k-token average load profile and share raw metrics.
2) I'll produce the first topology diagram + SLA sketch for your procurement team.
3) Sofia will draft the mutual action plan (MAP) with dates and responsibilities.

Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Quick technical addendum and attachments (attached: heliotrope-infra-diagram.pdf, heliotrope-sla-table.xlsx)

Hi all — following up with concrete bench plan and hypothesis so we can converge quickly:

Bench plan (Karthik)
- Run 3x repeatable runs per model variant (llama-3-chat-int8, distilled-7b-int8, 4-bit fallback) at token lengths [64, 256, 1024, 2000].
- Measure: TTFT (ms), throughput (tokens/sec), GPU utilization, memory pressure, cold-start recovery time.
- Run under two load profiles: steady 200 QPS and burst scenario simulating 1.2k QPS for 15 minutes.

Hypotheses
- Distilled-7b-int8 will meet TTFT 95th < 75ms for sub-100-token responses on A100 p4d-like instances.
- Llama-3-chat-int8 will provide higher-quality completions but may require larger dedicated pools to meet burst tail SLA.

Required inputs from Heliotrope
- Token histogram CSV and representative anonymized prompt set (Ari).
- Typical concurrency per user/session (helps with slot contention assumptions).

Next meeting proposal: Tuesday, Dec 5, 9:00 AM PST — 30 minutes to review initial bench results and MAP draft. If that works, procurement can circulate PO template and we can begin access provisioning.

Karthik Iyer
Staff Engineer (Inference) | Redwood Inference
